texts: After CABG, once chest tube drainage is acceptable, aspirin should be given within 6 hours of arrival in the ICU.
Early aspirin improves vein graft patency and lowers death, infarction and stroke after CABG, without a meaningful rise in bleeding.
A drainage of 70 mL per hour for two hours is modest and does not forbid it.
Waiting 24 hours loses much of the benefit for the vein grafts.
A second antiplatelet drug after an acute coronary syndrome is started once the bleeding risk settles, not as a clopidogrel load on arrival in the ICU.
In the picture, Chopper hands the little asp to the man as his gurney rolls in, before the hourglass with the Sitt painting runs out.
Memory hook: within six sand-hours, hand over the asp.
